sections.section: Outside · The building and the man
Museum · Origins and the first Cups

tracks.title: Welcome to the Bernabéu
tracks.where: Outside the stadium on the Paseo de la Castellana side, near the corner with Avenida de Concha Espina, where the club's tour entrance is. Anywhere you can see the curved steel bands of the facade will do.
tracks.what: What the Tour Bernabéu covers as of October 2026: the top-tier panoramic view, the museum, the home dressing room, the benches, the store; about two hours, many stairs; the two kinds of day that change the order; the pitch kept underground except for matches.
tracks.listen: What this visit is, the order it usually runs in, and what to do if your day is different.

tracks.section: Outside · The building and the man
tracks.title: Outside · The steel skin
tracks.where: Outside on the Paseo de la Castellana side, far enough back from the stadium to see the long curved bands of stainless steel running right around it.
tracks.what: The 2019 to 2026 rebuild of the 1947 stadium: gmp with L35 and Ribas & Ribas, competition won 2014, works from June 2019; home games at the Alfredo Di Stéfano stadium at the training ground until September 2021; the old building largely kept and wrapped in a stainless-steel louvre facade with gaps for natural ventilation; cost of about 1.4 billion to 30 June 2026 in the club's accounts.
tracks.listen: How the old stadium was kept and wrapped in a new steel skin while football went on, and what it cost.

tracks.section: Outside · The building and the man
tracks.title: Outside · Don Santiago's bet
tracks.where: Still outside on the Castellana side, with the steel facade in view. The stadium carries the name of the man in this story.
tracks.what: Santiago Bernabéu: player from boyhood to the late 1920s, president from 1943 until his death in 1978; the old Chamartín ground of about 25,000; first stone 27 October 1944; opening as Nuevo Chamartín on 14 December 1947, 3–1 v Os Belenenses, first goal Sabino Barinaga; 125,000 by 1954; named after him in 1955; six European Cups and sixteen league titles in his time; "Bernabéu" branding since late 2025.
tracks.listen: How a former player turned president built a stadium four times the size of the old one, and ended up giving it his name.

tracks.title: Panoramic · The view from the top
tracks.where: At the panoramic view in the top stands, the brochure's third tier, at the rail where the whole bowl opens out below you: the steep banks of seats, the roof overhead and the floor far down in the middle.
tracks.what: The bowl seen from the third tier; steep stands with no pillar in the way; no official capacity published, "around 80,000" (architects: access for up to about 83,000 at major events); the 125,000 of 1954 for comparison.
tracks.listen: Why nobody outside the club can tell you exactly how many people this bowl holds, and what you can see from the top of it.

tracks.title: Panoramic · From 1947 to now
tracks.where: At the panoramic level, by the scale model of the stadium and the screens showing the film of its transformation. If you can't reach them for the crowd, stay at the rail with the bowl in view.
tracks.what: The scale model and the club's audiovisual show on the stadium's transformation since 1947; finals played here: European Cup finals 1957 (Real Madrid 2–0 Fiorentina), 1969 and 1980; the 1964 European Championship final (Spain beat the USSR); the 1982 World Cup final (Italy 3–1 West Germany); the 2010 Champions League final (Inter 2–0 Bayern, coach José Mourinho, unveiled at Real Madrid days later); the 2018 Copa Libertadores final (River Plate v Boca Juniors).
tracks.listen: The model and film of the stadium's changes, and the great finals this ground has hosted, only one of them with Real Madrid on the pitch.

tracks.title: Panoramic · The roof and the ring
tracks.where: At the panoramic level, looking up: the roof spanning the stadium and, hanging below its inner edge, the continuous band of video screens that circles the whole bowl.
tracks.what: The retractable roof, 55 m above the ground, carried on supports in the towers on the Castellana and on Calle Padre Damián, closing in around a quarter of an hour; the roof steel as given by its fabricator; the 360° video scoreboard by Daktronics, 6.5 m high on the sides and corners, 11 m at the ends, tilted 8°, first used at the Clásico of 21 April 2024 (Real Madrid 3–2 Barcelona, Bellingham in stoppage time).
tracks.listen: How the roof stays up with no pillars in the stands, how long it takes to close, and the ring of screens that was switched on for a Clásico.

tracks.title: Panoramic · The pitch that goes underground
tracks.where: At the rail of the panoramic level, looking straight down at the floor of the stadium, which on most visiting days is bare or covered rather than green.
tracks.what: The retractable pitch: natural grass kept in six trays in the "hipogeo", the club's underground greenhouse, raised only for matches, a few hours to move; the floor used for other events, such as the first NFL regular-season game in Spain in November 2025; the 2024 concerts, the noise complaints, the suspension in September 2024 and the May 2026 Audiencia Provincial ruling.
tracks.listen: Why the floor below is usually bare, where the grass goes, and how the plan to fill this stadium with concerts ran into its neighbours.

tracks.title: Panoramic · Extra · Stage fright
tracks.where: Anywhere at the panoramic rail with the steep stands in view, before you leave the top tier for the museum.
tracks.what: "Miedo escénico", stage fright: the phrase Jorge Valdano popularised for what the Bernabéu does to visiting teams, borrowed from Gabriel García Márquez; his essay in Revista de Occidente, 1986; the UEFA Cup comeback against Borussia Mönchengladbach, 11 December 1985 (lost 5–1 away, won 4–0 here, through on away goals; Valdano 2, Santillana 2).
tracks.listen: Where the Bernabéu's famous "stage fright" comes from, and the comeback night behind it.

tracks.section: Museum · Origins and the first Cups
tracks.title: Museum · Into the museum
tracks.where: The first part of the museum, where the club's history begins: old photographs, early shirts and screens of archive film, before the route reaches the trophy hall.
tracks.what: The club's founding as Madrid Football Club, 6 March 1902; the royal title "Real" and the crown on the badge, granted by Alfonso XIII on 29 June 1920; ownership by the members, the socios; what kind of museum this is.
tracks.listen: How a plain Madrid Football Club became Real Madrid, who owns it, and how to get the best from a museum that is the club telling its own story.

tracks.section: Museum · Origins and the first Cups
tracks.title: Trophy hall · The fifteen
tracks.where: In the trophy hall, at the long row of European Cups, the big silver trophies with looping handles. Stand back far enough to take in the whole line at once.
tracks.what: The fifteen European Cups / Champions Leagues, 1956–2024; the latest at Wembley, 1 June 2024, 2–0 v Borussia Dortmund; the honours board (Milan 7, Liverpool 6, Bayern 6, Barcelona 5); the original trophy kept after 1966; PSG's 2025 and 2026 titles (dated).
tracks.listen: What fifteen European Cups means next to everyone else, and the small story of the original trophy.

tracks.section: Museum · Origins and the first Cups
tracks.title: Trophy hall · Di Stéfano and the first five
tracks.where: At the row of European Cups, by the five oldest trophies, the ones won in consecutive years from 1956 to 1960.
tracks.what: Five European Cups in a row, 1956–1960; Alfredo Di Stéfano (born Buenos Aires 1926, at the club 1953–1964, 308 goals in 396 matches) scoring in all five finals; the 1957 final played at this stadium, 2–0 v Fiorentina; Glasgow, 18 May 1960, 7–3 v Eintracht Frankfurt, Puskás 4, Di Stéfano 3, 127,000 crowd.
tracks.listen: The club's first golden age, the man at its centre, and the night in Glasgow that crowned it.

tracks.section: Museum · Origins and the first Cups
tracks.title: Trophy hall · Gento's six, and the Ye-yé
tracks.where: At the row of European Cups, by cup number six, the 1966 trophy, the one that comes straight after the five won in a row.
tracks.what: Paco Gento's six European Cups (1956–60 and 1966), eight finals, sole record holder 1966–2024, equalled in 2024 by Carvajal, Modrić, Nacho and Kroos; the 1966 final, Heysel, Brussels, 11 May 1966, 2–1 v Partizan (Vasović 55', Amancio 70', Serena 76'), coach Miguel Muñoz, eleven Spanish players; the "Ye-yé" name.
tracks.listen: The one player who was there for all six, and the new all-Spanish team, nicknamed after a Beatles chorus, that won the sixth.

tracks.section: Museum · Origins and the first Cups
tracks.title: Trophy hall · Thirty-two years, then La Séptima
tracks.where: At the row of European Cups, between cup number six, from 1966, and cup number seven, from 1998.
tracks.what: The 32-year gap, 1966–1998; the one final reached in between, Paris 1981, lost 1–0 to Liverpool; La Séptima: Amsterdam ArenA, 20 May 1998, 1–0 v Juventus, Predrag Mijatović 66', coach Jupp Heynckes.
tracks.listen: The long stretch when the club could not win in Europe, and the night in Amsterdam that ended it.

tracks.title: Trophy hall · Zidane's volley
tracks.where: At the row of European Cups, by cup number nine, the 2002 trophy won in Glasgow.
tracks.what: Cup eight, Paris 2000, 3–0 v Valencia; cup nine, Hampden Park, Glasgow, 15 May 2002, 2–1 v Bayer Leverkusen: Raúl 9', Lúcio 14', Zidane 44' left-foot volley from Roberto Carlos's looping cross from the left; the club's centenary year; Casillas on for the injured César at 68' and his late saves.
tracks.listen: One of the most celebrated goals in the club's history, scored on the same ground as the seven-three of 1960, and the young substitute keeper who saved the night.

tracks.title: Museum · The Galácticos
tracks.where: Still in the museum, close to the trophy hall. No single display is needed for this story: any spot with a view of the row of cups will do.
tracks.what: Florentino Pérez elected July 2000, beating Lorenzo Sanz, on a promise to sign Luís Figo from Barcelona; Zidane (2001, from Juventus), Ronaldo Nazário (2002, from Inter), Beckham (2003, from Manchester United); resigned 2006, returned 2009; contested re-election 7 June 2026, 65% to Enrique Riquelme's 35%, proclaimed 11 June 2026 for an eighth term to 2030 (dated).
tracks.listen: How one election promise started the era of the Galácticos, and the man who has shaped the club, and this stadium, ever since.

tracks.title: Trophy hall · La Décima
tracks.where: At the row of European Cups, by cup number ten, the 2014 trophy won in Lisbon.
tracks.what: La Décima: Lisbon, Benfica's stadium, 24 May 2014, Real Madrid 4–1 Atlético de Madrid after extra time. Godín 36'; Sergio Ramos header 93' (92:48 on the clock) from a Modrić corner; Bale 110', Marcelo 118', Cristiano Ronaldo 120' penalty. Captain Iker Casillas; coach Carlo Ancelotti.
tracks.listen: Twelve years of waiting, a city derby in a European final, and the header in the ninety-third minute that saved it.

tracks.title: Trophy hall · Three in a row, and Cristiano
tracks.where: At the row of European Cups, by cups eleven, twelve and thirteen, the trophies from 2016, 2017 and 2018.
tracks.what: Milan, San Siro, 28 May 2016, 1–1 v Atlético, 5–3 on penalties, Ronaldo the decisive kick; Cardiff, 3 June 2017, 4–1 v Juventus, first team to retain the Champions League; Kyiv, 26 May 2018, 3–1 v Liverpool, Benzema, Bale two incl. a bicycle kick; coach Zinedine Zidane; Cristiano Ronaldo 2009–2018, 451 goals in 438 matches, the club's all-time top scorer.
tracks.listen: How Zidane's team did what no side had done in the Champions League, and the goalscorer who carried it.

tracks.title: Trophy hall · 2022 and 2024
tracks.where: At the row of European Cups, by cups fourteen and fifteen, the trophies from 2022 and 2024.
tracks.what: The 2022 run: comebacks against Paris Saint-Germain, Chelsea and Manchester City; final, Stade de France, Paris, 28 May 2022, 1–0 v Liverpool, Vinícius Júnior 59', Courtois player of the match. Wembley, 1 June 2024, 2–0 v Borussia Dortmund, Carvajal and Vinícius. Carlo Ancelotti: first coach to win four, then five; 15 titles with the club, the most of any coach; left May 2025.
tracks.listen: A season of impossible comebacks, two finals won, and the coach who won more with this club than anyone.

tracks.title: Museum · The Ballon d'Or
tracks.where: In the museum, at the Ballon d'Or display: golden footballs shown in glass cases. If you can't spot it, any quiet corner near the trophies works for this story.
tracks.what: Ballon d'Or awards won while at Real Madrid, up to and including the 2025 award: 12 awards to 8 players (Di Stéfano 1957, 1959; Kopa 1958; Figo 2000; Ronaldo Nazário 2002; Cannavaro 2006; Cristiano Ronaldo 2013, 2014, 2016, 2017; Modrić 2018; Benzema 2022). The club's own wider list (11 players, 18 awards, incl. awards won elsewhere and Di Stéfano's 1989 Super Ballon d'Or). The 2024 ceremony the club did not attend.
tracks.listen: Who won football's best-known individual prize while wearing white, why you may hear two different totals, and the year the club stayed away.

tracks.title: Museum · Extra · The other Real Madrid
tracks.where: Anywhere in the museum, ideally at the area the club dedicates to its women's first team, or by any basketball trophies you pass. Both sit away from the long row of European Cups.
tracks.what: Real Madrid Baloncesto's eleventh European Cup, Kaunas, 21 May 2023, 79–78 v Olympiacos, Sergio Llull's basket with 3.1 seconds left; its first, 1964 v Spartak Brno; the 2026 final lost to Olympiacos, so still eleven as of autumn 2026. Real Madrid Femenino: built on CD Tacón, official from 1 July 2020; the museum's own area for the women's first team.
tracks.listen: The two other Real Madrids most visitors walk past: a basketball team with eleven European Cups, and a women's team only a few years old.

tracks.title: Museum · Extra · League, cup and the century
tracks.where: In the museum, wherever you find the league and cup trophies or the FIFA trophy for the best club of the 20th century, before you leave the museum.
tracks.what: 36 Ligas (first 1931–32, unbeaten, under the name Madrid F.C.) and 20 Copas del Rey (first 1905) as of autumn 2026; nine world club titles in the club's own count; the FIFA trophy for the best club of the 20th century, presented in Rome on 11 December 2000.
tracks.listen: The everyday trophies behind the European Cups, and the one award that covers a whole century.

tracks.title: Museum · Extra · Closed today?
tracks.where: At the end of the museum, before you move on. Play this if staff or the signs say the dressing room and benches are closed today, or if your route took you through the museum first.
tracks.what: The club closes the dressing rooms and benches on match days and the day before; a short picture of the first-team dressing room (the 15-minute half-time interval in the Laws of the Game) and of the benches at pitch level; where the route goes instead.
tracks.listen: What lies behind the two doors that close on match days, and where to go from here.

tracks.title: Dressing room · The home dressing room
tracks.where: Inside the first-team dressing room, the home side's room, standing anywhere you can see the players' seats around the walls.
tracks.what: The Vestuario del Primer Equipo (first-team, home dressing room), closed to visitors on match days and the day before; the half-time interval of at most 15 minutes in the Laws of the Game; half-time here on 9 March 2022, Real Madrid one down to Paris Saint-Germain, two down on aggregate.
tracks.listen: The one room on the tour that still has a job to do, and what fifteen minutes in it can mean.

tracks.title: Benches · The view from the bench
tracks.where: At pitch level, by the team benches beside the playing area, with the stands rising all around you.
tracks.what: Miguel Muñoz, captain of the first European Cup winners, then coach for 14 consecutive years from 1960 (605 matches, 14 titles); Carlo Ancelotti matching that record on 14 August 2024 and leaving in May 2025 with 15, the most in club history; Xabi Alonso (June 2025 to January 2026), Álvaro Arbeloa (January to June 2026); José Mourinho, coach since June 2026, second spell (first 2010–13); the stadium seen from pitch level.
tracks.listen: Who has sat on this bench, how long the seat has been kept, and what the stadium looks like from the bottom.

tracks.title: Benches · The late comebacks
tracks.where: Still at pitch level by the benches, looking out across the playing area to the stands opposite.
tracks.what: Champions League nights at the Bernabéu: v Paris Saint-Germain, 9 March 2022 (Benzema 61', 76', 78', 3–1, through 3–2 on aggregate); v Manchester City, 4 May 2022 (Rodrygo 90' and 90+1', Benzema penalty 95' in extra time, 6–5 on aggregate); v Bayern Munich, 8 May 2024 (Davies 68', Joselu 88' and 90+1', 2–1, 4–3 on aggregate); v Manchester City, 11 March 2026 (Valverde first-half hat-trick, 3–0); 2025-26 ended without a trophy; Valverde captain as of autumn 2026.
tracks.listen: Four famous nights in this stadium, most of them turned around late, and an honest word on what comebacks don't guarantee.

tracks.title: Press room · Extra · The press room
tracks.where: Only if the press room is open on your visit: inside it, anywhere you can see the front of the room, where the questions are answered.
tracks.what: The press room, offered by the club only as a temporary visit "subject to availability"; what a press conference here is; UEFA's Champions League rule that each club holds a press conference the day before a match with its head coach and at least one player, the visiting club normally in the match stadium.
tracks.listen: Why the person talking in this room the night before a big European game is often the visiting coach.

tracks.title: Store · The white shirt
tracks.where: In the official store at the end of the tour, anywhere you can see the racks and walls of white home shirts.
tracks.what: Why Real Madrid plays in white (the Corinthian story, told as a story; the club's own history of its early years doesn't explain it); the shirt as identity and business: record revenue of 1,221 million euros in 2025-26 per the club's July 2026 accounts; top of the Deloitte Football Money League for the third year running (January 2026); stadium revenue 363 million euros; a club owned by its members.
tracks.listen: How a colour borrowed, the story goes, from English amateurs became the uniform of one of the richest clubs in the world.

tracks.title: The way out, and goodbye
tracks.where: At the end of the store, as you leave the stadium. If the street sign outside says Calle Padre Damián, you are on the stadium's east side, opposite the Castellana side where you came in.
tracks.what: The tour ends in the store; the exit street, likely Calle Padre Damián (on-site check); Metro Line 10 suspended between Cuzco and Nuevos Ministerios, including the stadium's station, until the end of 2026, new station due in early 2027; the free S10 replacement bus on the Paseo de la Castellana by Plaza de Lima; Cercanías and Metro lines 6 and 8 at Nuevos Ministerios; a short send-off.
tracks.listen: How to get away from the stadium while its metro station is closed, and a last look back at the visit.
